chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about yawning during the Adhan and the Iqamah, so he said: 'We do not recognize it.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about yawning during the Adhan and Iqamah?
ai.summary: Muawiya ibn Wahb inquired of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the specific reward (thawab) for yawning during the Adhan and Iqamah, to which the Imam replied, 'We do not know it.' This response highlights the Shia scholarly principle of distinguishing between established, narrated virtues and those that are merely cultural or speculative, suggesting that while yawning is a natural physiological response, it does not carry a distinct, revealed merit in the ritual context of the call to prayer.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the yawning during the Azān and the Iqamah, so heasws said: ‘Weasws do not recognise (experience) it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following: “
I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about tathwib (yawning) in Adhan and ‘Iqamah. He (the Imam) said, ‘We do not know it (experience it).”’
